templates.text: No. This is an education tool, not financial advice. It shows what your own numbers suggest, in plain words. For big decisions, talk to a fee-only adviser who must act in your interest.

templates.label: app/agents/intake_answers.py:166
templates.text: I can only help with your retirement plan here.

templates.label: app/agents/intake_answers.py:13
templates.text: A Roth account (Roth IRA or Roth 401(k)) is saved from pay after tax. The money grows, and withdrawals in retirement are tax-free if the rules are met.

templates.label: app/agents/intake_answers.py:14
templates.text: A 401(k) is a retirement account through your employer. You save from your pay before tax, often with a match from the employer, and pay tax when you take the money out. A 403(b) or 457(b) works much the same way.

templates.label: app/agents/intake_answers.py:15
templates.text: An IRA is an individual retirement account you open yourself. A traditional IRA is usually saved before tax and taxed when you take money out; a Roth IRA is the reverse.

templates.label: app/agents/intake_answers.py:16
templates.text: Pre-tax means the money went in before income tax, as in a 401(k) or traditional IRA. You pay the tax when you take it out.

templates.label: app/agents/intake_answers.py:17
templates.text: A taxable account is an ordinary investment account, such as a brokerage account. It has no special tax shelter.

templates.label: app/agents/intake_answers.py:18
templates.text: A brokerage account is an ordinary investment account for stocks and funds. It has no special tax shelter.

templates.label: app/agents/intake_answers.py:19
templates.text: The mortgage balance is what you still owe on the loan. The payment is what you pay each month. The balance tells the plan when the mortgage ends; the payment tells it what you spend until then.

templates.label: app/agents/intake_answers.py:20
templates.text: The mortgage payment is what you pay the lender each month. The balance is what you still owe in total.

templates.label: app/agents/intake_answers.py:21
templates.text: Medicare is the federal health insurance for people 65 and older. Before 65, retirees pay for their own cover, which the plan counts as a cost.

templates.label: app/agents/intake_answers.py:22
templates.text: Social Security is the monthly benefit from the federal government, based on your earnings record. The later you claim, up to 70, the bigger the check. Your own estimate is at ssa.gov/myaccount.

templates.label: app/agents/intake_answers.py:23
templates.text: A pension is a regular payment from a former employer for life, usually from a set age. It is different from a 401(k), which is a pot of savings.

templates.label: app/agents/intake_answers.py:24
templates.text: A scenario is one possible path for markets over your life. The plan tries many and counts how often your money lasts, so its answers are chances, not promises.

templates.label: app/agents/intake_answers.py:25
templates.text: An employer match is money your employer adds to your 401(k) when you save, for example 50 cents per dollar up to a share of pay. It is the best return most people can get.

templates.label: app/agents/intake_answers.py:26
templates.text: An emergency fund is cash set aside for surprises, such as a job loss or a big repair, so you do not have to sell investments at a bad time.

templates.label: app/agents/intake_answers.py:27
templates.text: An annuity is a contract with an insurer: you pay a sum and get a regular income back, often for life.

templates.label: app/agents/intake_answers.py:28
templates.text: A required minimum distribution is the amount you must take out of pre-tax accounts each year from a set age.

templates.label: app/agents/intake_answers.py:29
templates.text: Net worth is what you own minus what you owe.

templates.label: app/agents/intake_answers.py:36
templates.text: Your age sets how many years you have left to save and how long the money must last.

templates.label: app/agents/intake_answers.py:37
templates.text: Your partner's age sets how long the money must last for both of you.

templates.label: app/agents/intake_answers.py:38
templates.text: Your state sets your taxes and the typical cost of living, which the plan uses for your basics.

templates.label: app/agents/intake_answers.py:39
templates.text: Your pay sets your taxes, how much you can save, and your Social Security.

templates.label: app/agents/intake_answers.py:40
templates.text: Your partner's pay adds to what you can save and to the household's Social Security.

templates.label: app/agents/intake_answers.py:41
templates.text: Your savings are the money the plan draws on once you stop working.

templates.label: app/agents/intake_answers.py:42
templates.text: Children's ages tell the plan when their costs end and when college comes.

templates.label: app/agents/intake_answers.py:43
templates.text: Housing is most people's biggest cost. A mortgage ends; rent does not.

templates.label: app/agents/intake_answers.py:44
templates.text: The balance and the payment tell the plan when the mortgage ends and your costs fall.

templates.label: app/agents/intake_answers.py:45
templates.text: Debts cost interest and take part of your pay until they are paid off.

templates.label: app/agents/intake_answers.py:46
templates.text: It is the goal the plan tests: whether your money lasts if you stop then.

templates.label: app/agents/intake_answers.py:47
templates.text: Spending is what your money must cover, now and in retirement.

templates.label: app/agents/intake_answers.py:145
templates.text: Your plan will answer that with your own numbers. It needs a few more answers first.

templates.label: app/agents/intake_answers.py:149
templates.text: I mean everything the household pays for in a normal year: rent or mortgage, food, car, insurance, health care and the rest. A rough monthly figure is fine.

templates.label: app/agents/intake_answers.py:150
templates.text: I mean what you expect to spend each year once you stop working, in today's dollars.

templates.label: app/agents/intake_answers.py:151
templates.text: I mean everything put away: 401(k)s, IRAs, other investments and cash in the bank, added up. A rough total is fine.
